findings.evidence: List of Figures entry: '1 The architect's decision loop — the book's spine . . . ix' and '2 Reading the book two ways . . . x' — these are the only two entries that carry page numbers; every subsequent entry (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, … 26.2, A.1–A.5) is listed with dots but no page number in the extracted text.
findings.issue: The List of Figures is inconsistent: figures 1 and 2 carry page numbers (ix, x) while figures 1.1–A.5 carry none. Either every LoF entry needs a page number or the convention should be uniform. (Confirm on the rendered page whether the numbers are truly absent rather than lost in extraction.)
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate the List of Figures so that every entry ends with its page number, or explicitly state a convention that only front-matter figures are paginated.

findings.evidence: Contents (pp. i–ii) lists chapters, parts, Appendix A, Glossary, References, Sources/Method, and The Architecture Worksheet, but there is no List of Tables anywhere in the front matter; the Contents page footer sequence is i, ii then the List of Figures begins at iii.
findings.issue: The book contains at least 20 numbered tables (Table 1-1, 2-1, 2-2, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3, 4-1, 4-2, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1, 7-1, 7-2, 7-3, 8-1, …) yet provides no List of Tables. Readers cannot navigate tables, and the figure/table ontology is asymmetric.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a List of Tables after the List of Figures, or state explicitly in the front matter why tables are not indexed.

findings.evidence: Contents (pp. 7-8) lists Part I 'The Token' with chapters 1-3 and page numbers 2, 15, 35; Part II 'The Workload' chapters 4-6 at pages 56, 91, 108; Part III 'The System' chapters 7-11 at 122, 153, 175, 193, 206; Part IV 'The Architecture' chapters 12-16 at 226, 244, 253, 264, 284; Part V 'The Fleet' chapters 17-21 at 311, 337, 352, 376, 390; Part VI 'The Architect' chapters 22-26 at 397, 409, 416, 431, 446; Appendix A at 466, Glossary 499, References 504, Sources/Method 507, Worksheet 515. The Preface occupies printed pages vi-xiv (PDF pp. 12-20).
findings.issue: Printed-folio versus PDF-index offset and a broken Contents sequence. Every Contents page number is the printed folio, which is offset from the PDF index by +6 (e.g. Ch. 1's printed folio 2 is PDF p. 22; Ch. 4's printed 56 is PDF p. 76; Ch. 8's printed 153 is PDF p. 173; the Preface's printed vi is PDF p. 12). A reader who treats the Contents numbers as PDF positions lands 6 pages early everywhere, and the offset is never stated. Worse, the Contents omits the front-matter apparatus entirely: there is no 'List of Figures' or 'List of Tables' entry, and the List of Figures that exists (pp. 9-11) has no counterpart List of Tables even though the book contains numbered tables throughout (Table 2-1, 2-2, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3, 4-1, 4-2, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1, 7-1, 7-2, 7-3, 8-1 …). The Contents also lists 'Preface . . . vi' but the Preface's own Figures 1 and 2 are listed in the List of Figures with folios 'ix' and 'x' — consistent with folios, not with the PDF index.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a one-line note under the Contents: 'Page numbers are printed folios; the PDF index runs 6 higher (printed p. 1 = PDF p. 7).' Add a 'List of Tables' section mirroring the List of Figures (with folio numbers), and add List of Figures / List of Tables entries to the Contents itself so the front-matter apparatus is navigable.

findings.evidence: List of Figures (pp. 9-11) entries with folios: '1.1 The KV cache: every token adds one K/V per layer per head . . . 9'; '1.2 How a token travels: text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention → KV cache . . . 10'; '2.1 The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline, in two process bands plus the… . . . 20'; '7.5 KV cache size vs context length, canonical 80-layer reference geometry . . . 147'; 'A.2 Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios . . . 475'.
findings.issue: List-of-Figures entry titles are truncated mid-sentence or mid-word relative to the actual captions, so the LoF is not a reliable index: '2.1 The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline, in two process bands plus the…' is cut (the caption on p. 40 continues '…plus the persistent KV cache'); '7.1 Grouped-Query Attention cuts per-token KV' vs the caption's 'Figure 7.1: Grouped-Query Attention cuts per-token KV' (this one matches) but '4.1 Six workload dimensions and the architectural decisions each one informs' (LoF) vs the caption 'Six workload dimensions and the architectural decision each one drives' (p. 106) — singular/plural mismatch. Also '11.2 Serving is four separable concerns, not a stack (they interact . . .' is truncated without an ellipsis. Independently, the LoF folios cannot be reconciled against the PDF index (offset +6): '1.1 … 9' is PDF p. 29, '1.2 … 10' is PDF p. 30, '2.1 … 20' is PDF p. 40 — so the folio offsets are internally consistent with the printed folios, which is the same pagination defect as PA-001 and shows the LoF needs the same note.
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate the List of Figures from the actual captions so every title is complete and identical to its caption's title text (fix 'decision each one drives' vs 'decisions each one informs' and complete the truncated '2.1', '11.2' entries), and add the folio-versus-PDF-index note to the List of Figures as well as the Contents.

findings.evidence: Contents (PDF 7–8) and the List of Figures (PDF 9–11) contain no List of Tables, although the visible pages alone carry 14+ numbered, load-bearing tables — e.g. "Table 4-2 — Canonical-scenario provenance ledger ... This is the authority for which is which" (PDF 89), plus Tables 2-1, 2-2, 3-1–3-3, 4-1, 5-1, 5-2, 6-1, 7-1–7-3, 8-1.
findings.issue: Navigation asymmetry in a reference handbook: figures are indexed but the tables that carry the book's canonical constants and provenance authority (Table 4-2 is declared 'the one authoritative set of numbers') are not. Possible the SM&R/back matter compensates, but within the verifiable range no table index exists.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a List of Tables (with book page numbers, matching the List of Figures format) after the List of Figures, or state in the Contents why tables are deliberately unindexed.
